Lindsay has written several books including ''[[Cynical Theories]]'' (2020), which he co-authored with Pluckrose. He has promoted [[Right-wing politics|right-wing]] [[conspiracy theories]] such as [[Cultural Marxism conspiracy theory|Cultural Marxism]], [[White genocide]], and [[LGBT grooming conspiracy theories|LGBT grooming]].<ref name="continued" /><ref name="Moyer 2023" /><ref name="Skopic 2022" /><ref name="Conway 2021" />

==Early life and career==
James Stephen Lindsay was born in [[Ogdensburg, New York]]. He moved to [[Maryville, Tennessee]], at the age of five, later graduating from [[Maryville High School (Tennessee)|Maryville High School]] in 1997. Lindsay received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in [[physics]] and a [[Master of Science|M.S.]] in [[mathematics]] at [[Tennessee Tech]], and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mathematics in 2010 at the [[University of Tennessee|University of Tennessee, Knoxville]].{{sfn|Lindsay|2010|p=93}} His doctoral thesis is titled "Combinatorial Unification of Binomial-Like Arrays", and his advisor was Carl G. Wagner.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Lindsay|first=James|date=May 1, 2010|title=Combinatorial Unification of Binomial-Like Arrays|type=Doctor of Philosophy|url=https://trace.tennessee.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1803&context=utk_graddiss|publisher=[[University of Tennessee]] |journal=Doctoral Dissertations}}</ref> After completing his degree, Lindsay left academia and returned to his hometown, where he worked as a massage therapist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Joel |title=Maryville man walks path of healing and combat |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425235616/https://www.thedailytimes.com/news/maryville-man-walks-path-of-healing-and-combat/article_5ea3c0ca-2e98-5283-9e59-06861b8588cb.html |archive-date=April 25, 2022 |url=https://www.thedailytimes.com/news/maryville-man-walks-path-of-healing-and-combat/article_5ea3c0ca-2e98-5283-9e59-06861b8588cb.html |access-date=May 16, 2022 |website=The Daily Times |date=May 7, 2012 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="wants">{{Cite web |date=May 18, 2021 |title=Why grievance studies hoaxer and atheist James Lindsay wants to save Southern Baptists |url=https://religionnews.com/2021/05/18/james-lindsay-southern-baptists-crt-al-mohler-hoax-new-discourses-beth-moorerace-ofallon/ |access-date=July 3, 2022 |website=Religion News Service |language=en-US |quote=The hoax got the attention of Michael O'Fallon, a conservative activist and president of Sovereign Nations, a conservative Christian nationalist group.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=James Lindsay |url=https://www.splcenter.org/fighting-hate/extremist-files/individual/james-lindsay |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=Southern Poverty Law Center |language=en}}</ref>

Lindsay, along with [[Peter Boghossian]], is the co-author of ''How to Have Impossible Conversations: A Very Practical Guide'',<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Boghossian|first1=Peter G.|title=How to have impossible conversations: a very practical guide|date=2019|last2=Lindsay|first2=James A.|isbn=978-0738285320|edition=First|publisher=Life Long|location=New York|oclc=1085584392}}</ref> a nonfiction book released in 2019 and published by [[Lifelong Books]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=How to have impossible conversations|url=https://www.spiked-online.com/2019/11/01/how-to-have-impossible-conversations/|access-date=November 7, 2020|website=spiked-online.com|language=en}}</ref> In 2020, Lindsay released the nonfiction book ''[[Cynical Theories]]'', co-authored with [[Helen Pluckrose]] and published by [[Pitchstone Publishing]]. ==Grievance studies affair==
{{main|Grievance studies affair}}
[[File:Thumbnail of video Academics expose corruption in Grievance Studies.jpg|right|thumb|Lindsay and Pluckrose laughing at their grievance studies papers, in 2018]]
In 2017, Lindsay and Boghossian published a [[hoax]] paper titled "The Conceptual Penis as a Social Construct".<ref name="Schuessler 2018" /> In writing the paper, Lindsay and Boghossian intended to imitate the style of "[[Post-structuralism|poststructuralist]] discursive gender theory". The paper argued that the penis should be seen "not as an anatomical organ but as a social construct isomorphic to [[Performativity|performative]] [[toxic masculinity]]".<ref name="Schuessler 2018" /><ref>{{cite news|last1= Jaschik|first1=Scott|date=May 22, 2017|title=Hoax With Multiple Targets |work=Inside Higher Ed|url= https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2017/05/22/faux-scholarly-article-sets-criticism-gender-studies-and-open-access-publishing |access-date= January 23, 2019}}</ref> After the paper was rejected by ''[[Norma (journal)|Norma]],'' they later submitted it to ''Cogent Social Sciences'' where it was accepted for publication.<ref name="Schuessler 2018" /><ref>{{cite web|last1=Tillberg|first1=Anneli|date=June 12, 2017|title=Attack on gender studies despite rejection of hoax article|url=https://www.genus.se/en/newspost/attack-on-gender-studies-despite-rejection-of-hoax-article|access-date=April 17, 2019|website=Genus|archive-date=May 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512171052/https://www.genus.se/en/newspost/attack-on-gender-studies-despite-rejection-of-hoax-article/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=May 26, 2017|title=Statement regarding hoax article|url=https://normajournal.wordpress.com/2017/05/26/statement-regarding-hoax-article/|access-date=April 17, 2019|website=Norma: International Journal for Masculinity Studies|archive-date=April 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413185923/https://normajournal.wordpress.com/2017/05/26/statement-regarding-hoax-article/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Beauchamp |first=Zack |title=The controversy around hoax studies in critical theory, explained |url=https://www.vox.com/2018/10/15/17951492/grievance-studies-sokal-squared-hoax |newspaper=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |date=October 15, 2018 |access-date=February 17, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181015200241/https://www.vox.com/2018/10/15/17951492/grievance-studies-sokal-squared-hoax#:~:text=mathematician%20James%20Lindsay|archive-date=2018-10-15|url-status=live}}</ref>

Beginning in August 2017, Lindsay, Boghossian, and Pluckrose wrote 20 additional 'woke' hoax papers, which they submitted to peer-reviewed journals using several pseudonyms as well as the name of Richard Baldwin, a friend of Boghossian and professor emeritus of history at Florida's [[Gulf Coast State College]]. The project ended early after one of the papers, published in the feminist geography journal ''[[Gender, Place & Culture]]'', was questioned by investigative journalist Toni Airaksinen of ''[[Campus Reform]]'' who suspected the article was not real due to its lack of adherence to academic journal publishing standards. This resulted in widespread interest in the incident, which was written about by several journalists.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 25, 2018 |title=Academic journal duped by author of 'dog rape culture' article|language=en-US |author= Toni Airaksinen |work= Campus Reform |url= https://www.campusreform.org/?ID=11158 |access-date= August 10, 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181009132026/https://www.campusreform.org/?ID=11158 |archive-date= October 9, 2018}}</ref>

The trio subsequently revealed the full scope of their work in a [[YouTube]] video created and released by documentary filmmaker [[Mike Nayna]], which was accompanied by an investigation by ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|last= Melchior|first=Jillian Kay|date= October 5, 2018|title=Fake News Comes to Academia|language=en-US|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url= https://www.wsj.com/articles/fake-news-comes-to-academia-1538520950 |access-date=October 8, 2018|issn= 0099-9660}}</ref> By the time of this revelation, seven of their twenty papers had been accepted, seven were still under review, and six had been rejected. One paper, accepted by feminist social work journal ''[[Affilia]]'', contained passages copied from [[Adolf Hitler]]'s ''[[Mein Kampf]]'' with feminist language added,<ref name="Schuessler 2018">{{Cite news| last = Schuessler | first = Jennifer|date= October 4, 2018|title=Hoaxers Slip Breastaurants and Dog-Park Sex Into Journals |work=[[The New York Times]] |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2018/10/04/arts/academic-journals-hoax.html |access-date=October 8, 2018 |quote= …a third paper, published in a journal of feminist social work and titled 'Our Struggle Is My Struggle,' simply scattered some up-to-date jargon into passages lifted from Hitler's 'Mein Kampf…' They set out to write 20 papers that started with 'politically fashionable conclusions,' which they worked backward to support by aping the relevant fields' methods and arguments, and sometimes inventing data.}}</ref> though sociologist {{ill |Mikko Lagerspetz|fi}} has contended that the paper only contained similarities in structure, and did not contain material "historically specific in Hitler's text (racism, references to the [[World War I|First World War]], and so on)".<ref>{{Cite journal|last= Lagerspetz|first=Mikko|date=May 5, 2020|title="The Grievance Studies Affair" Project: Reconstructing and Assessing the Experimental Design |journal=Science, Technology, & Human Values |volume= 46|issue=2|pages=402–424|doi= 10.1177/0162243920923087|issn= 0162-2439|doi-access=free}}</ref> Academic reviewers had praised the hoax studies of Lindsay, Boghossian, and Pluckrose as "a rich and exciting contribution to the study of&nbsp;... the intersection between masculinity and anality", "excellent and very timely", and "important dialogue for social workers and feminist scholars".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Whipple|first1=Tom|date=October 4, 2018|title=Journals publish hoaxers' absurd gender studies|page=19|work= [[The Times]] |url= https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/property-home/article/journals-publish-hoaxers-absurd-gender-studies-q7f60l7v6|url-access=subscription|access-date=January 27, 2019|via=[[EBSCOhost]] Newspaper Source Plus}}</ref>

==Views==
Prior to 2020, Lindsay supported [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] candidates, including volunteering for [[Barack Obama]], and was part of the [[New Atheism]] movement.<ref name="Joyce 2022">{{cite web | last=Joyce | first= Kathryn | title=Meet James Lindsay, the far right's "world-level expert" on CRT and "Race Marxism" | website=Salon | date=February 17, 2022 | url= https://www.salon.com/2022/02/17/meet-james-lindsay-the-far-rights-world-level-expert-on-crt-and-race-marxism/ | access-date=February 23, 2022}}</ref> In 2023, Lindsay published an article on New Discourses in which he set out to defend the philosophical basis of [[classical liberalism]], which he summarized as "the project of organizing our society from a position of political equality with certain rights that are inalienable, among these life, liberty, property, capacity for their use toward our happiness and purposes, and a reasonable expectation of privacy in which we can maintain their sanctity".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=James |date=2023-11-10 |title=The Basis of Classical Liberalism |url=https://newdiscourses.com/2023/11/basis-of-classical-liberalism/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110195142/https://newdiscourses.com/2023/11/basis-of-classical-liberalism/ |archive-date=2023-11-10 |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=New Discourses |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lindsay is a critic of "[[wokeness]]", which he analogizes to [[religious]] belief.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Romano|first=Aja|date= October 9, 2020 |title=How being 'woke' lost its meaning|url= https://www.vox.com/culture/21437879/stay-woke-wokeness-history-origin-evolution-controversy|access-date=November 7, 2020|website=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]}}</ref> He describes "the [[Social Justice]] Movement" as his "ideological enemy".<ref>{{cite web|last1= Lindsay|first1=James|title=Naming the Enemy: Critical Social Justice|url= https://newdiscourses.com/2020/02/naming-enemy-critical-social-justice/|access-date=November 9, 2020|website=New Discourses|date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Though he opposed [[Donald Trump]] in the [[2016 United States presidential election]], Lindsay announced his intention to vote for Trump in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 election]], arguing that the danger of "wokeness" is much greater than that of a Trump presidency.<ref>{{cite web|last= Mounk|first=Yascha|date=October 26, 2020|title=Trump Is the Best Candidate for the Illiberal Left|url= https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2020/10/hate-wokeness-vote-biden/616845/|access-date=January 11, 2021|work=[[The Atlantic]]}}</ref> In 2024, he voted again for Donald Trump.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lindsay|first=James|date=October 18, 2024|title=Another vote for President Trump! Lines were long all day. People are turning out to vote in tremendous numbers.|url=https://twitter.com/i/status/1847400612822208522|work=Twitter}}</ref>

Lindsay has clashed with other right-wing figures, who he refers to as the "[[woke right]]".<ref name=":1">{{cite news |last=Tomco |first=Brigham |title=Is there a 'woke right'? |url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/05/06/james-lindsay-and-jordan-peterson-explain-the-woke-right/ |newspaper=[[Deseret News]] |date=May 6, 2025 |access-date=July 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507033427/https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/05/06/james-lindsay-and-jordan-peterson-explain-the-woke-right/#:~:text=James%20Lindsay%2C%20%E2%80%9Cauthor%2C%20mathematician|archive-date=2025-05-07|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Beauchamp |first=Zach |title=The anti-woke right won in 2024. Now they're turning on each other |url=https://www.vox.com/on-the-right-newsletter/412988/curtis-yarvin-scott-alexander-woke-right-james-lindsay |newspaper=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |date=May 14, 2025 |access-date=July 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250515143240/https://www.vox.com/on-the-right-newsletter/412988/curtis-yarvin-scott-alexander-woke-right-james-lindsay |archive-date=May 15, 2025 }}</ref> [[Southern Baptist Theological Seminary]] president [[Albert Mohler]] looked to Lindsay to understand critical race theory<ref name="wants" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mohler |first=R. Albert |author-link=Albert Mohler |date=September 2, 2020 |title=Critical Theory and the Cynical Transformation of Society: A Conversation with James Lindsay |url=https://albertmohler.com/2020/09/02/james-lindsay |website=albertmohler.com}}</ref> because, in Mohler's words, few have "given sustained attention to critical theory from a conservative viewpoint".<ref name="wants" />

===Conspiracy theory promotion===
Lindsay has promoted several conspiracy theories.<ref name="continued">{{Cite web |date=July 5, 2021 |title=Counterweight, and the continued enabling of bad faith 'anti-woke' actors |url=https://www.skeptic.org.uk/2021/07/counterweight-and-the-continued-enabling-of-bad-faith-anti-woke-actors/ |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=The Skeptic |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="Conway 2021">{{cite journal|first1=Philip R.|last1=Conway|title=Critical international politics at an impasse: reflexivist, reformist, reactionary, and restitutive post-critique|url=https://doi.org/10.1057/s41312-021-00111-3|journal=International Politics Reviews|date=1 June 2021|issn=2050-2990|pages=213–238|volume=9|issue=1|doi=10.1057/s41312-021-00111-3|s2cid=256552762 |quote=[Lindsay] has also taken to promoting the conspiracy theory that global elites are enacting a vast, diabolical “plan” to reduce “world population to under 2B[illion], perhaps by the end of the decade” (2021a) – a task to which the insidious grievance-mongering of critical academics is apparently essential. Only one 'Enlightenment'-loving conspiracist among many others, these views are propounded from the bully's pulpit of a 201,000-follower Twitter account (at the time of writing).|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He is a proponent of the [[LGBT grooming conspiracy theory]] and has been credited as one of several public figures responsible for popularizing "[[Sexual grooming|groomer]]" as a slur directed at [[LGBTQ]] educators and activists by members of the political right.<ref name="brings">{{cite web|accessdate=2024-01-14|title=Elon Musk's 'amnesty' pledge brings back QAnon, far-right Twitter accounts|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/internet/elon-musks-twitter-beginning-take-shape-rcna58940|date=2 December 2022|website=NBC News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Right-wing 'groomer' attacks target suicide prevention service for LGBTQ youth |url= https://news.yahoo.com/right-wing-groomer-attacks-target-suicide-prevention-service-for-lgbtq-youth-130037286.html |access-date= May 16, 2022 |website= News |date= May 4, 2022 | publisher = Yahoo |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date= April 27, 2022 |title=How the Intellectual Dark Web Spawned 'Groomer' Panic |work=The Daily Beast |url= https://www.thedailybeast.com/how-the-intellectual-dark-web-spawned-anti-lgbtq-groomer-panic |access-date= May 16, 2022}}</ref> Lindsay has referred to the [[Pride flag]] as "the flag of a hostile enemy".<ref name="Moyer 2023">{{Cite news |last=Moyer|first=Josh|date=April 22, 2023 |title= Two events featuring controversial right-wing speakers at Penn State are canceled|language=en |work=Centre Daily|url=https://www.centredaily.com/news/local/education/penn-state/article274581401.html|access-date=January 1, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Fisher 2022">{{Cite news |last=Fisher |first=Anthony L. |date=August 9, 2022 |title=The Banned 'OK Groomer' Guy Is Not a Free-Speech Martyr |language=en |work=The Daily Beast |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/the-banned-ok-groomer-guy-james-lindsay-is-not-a-free-speech-martyr |access-date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

In 2021, Lindsay wrote on Twitter that "there will be" a [[genocide]] of [[White people|whites]] if [[critical race theory]] "isn't stopped."<ref name="Woodruff 2021">{{Cite web |last=Woodruff |first=Chase |date=June 12, 2021 |title=Ousted Space Force commander defended by Rep. Lamborn advanced white 'genocide' theory in book |url=https://coloradonewsline.com/2021/06/12/ousted-space-force-commander-defended-by-rep-lamborn-advanced-white-genocide-theory-in-book/ |access-date=October 31, 2022 |website=Colorado Newsline |language=en-US |quote=James Lindsay, a well-known right-wing academic whose work Lohmeier cites in his book, faced criticism from many of his fellow conservatives last week after writing on Twitter that "there will be" a genocide of whites "if this ideology isn’t stopped." Earlier this month, Lindsay was a featured panelist at the annual retreat of the Leadership Program of the Rockies, a conservative networking organization, at The Broadmoor resort in Colorado Springs. "James Lindsay is now peddling White Genocide Theory," Claire Lehmann, founder of the right-leaning website Quillette, wrote on Twitter on June 9. "Implying that a genocide against whites in the U.S. is imminent has the potential to inspire racist violence. Such comments are extreme, reckless, and irresponsible. They should be denounced."}}</ref> His statement was met with widespread criticism, including from founder of [[libertarian]] anti-[[identity politics]] magazine ''[[Quillette]]'' [[Claire Lehmann]] who wrote: "James Lindsay is now peddling [[White genocide conspiracy theory|White Genocide Theory]]. Implying that a genocide against whites in the U.S. is imminent has the potential to inspire racist violence. Such comments are extreme, reckless, and irresponsible. They should be denounced."<ref name="Woodruff 2021" /><ref>{{Cite tweet |last=Lehmann |first=Claire |user=clairlemon |number=1402771614631006208 |date=June 9, 2021|title=James Lindsay is now peddling White Genocide Theory. Implying that a genocide against whites in the US is imminent has the potential to inspire racist violence. Such comments are extreme, reckless, & irresponsible. They should be denounced. |language=en |access-date=|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220501161818/https://twitter.com/clairlemon/status/1402771614631006208 |archive-date=May 1, 2022}}</ref> Lindsay has also promoted the far-right [[Cultural Marxism conspiracy theory]],<ref name="Weigel 2023">{{cite journal|first1=Moira|last1=Weigel|title=Hating Theory: "Cultural Marxism," "CRT," and the Power of Media Affects|url=https://ijoc.org/index.php/ijoc/article/view/21427|journal=International Journal of Communication|date=29 October 2023|issn=1932-8036|pages=21|volume=17}}</ref><ref name="Joyce 2022" /><ref name="Skopic 2022">{{Cite news |last=Skopic |first=Alex |date=December 1, 2022 |title=James Lindsay's "Race Marxism" is Ignorant About Both Race and Marxism |language=en |work=Current Affairs |url=https://www.currentaffairs.org/news/2022/12/james-lindsays-race-marxism-is-ignorant-about-both-race-and-marxism |access-date=January 16, 2023 |issn=2471-2647}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=James Lindsay |url=https://www.splcenter.org/fighting-hate/extremist-files/individual/james-lindsay |website=splcenter.org |publisher=The [[Southern Poverty Law Center]] |access-date=2 February 2024}}</ref> which alleges a concerted effort by [[Critical theorists|Marxist critical theorists]] to undermine [[Western culture|Western civilization]] using Marxism.<ref name="Skopic 2022" /><ref name="Weigel 2023" />
